\chapter{Complexity — Time Constructible}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.TimeConstructible
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module defines time-constructible functions in the sense of Arora--Barak
\S1.3: a time bound $T$ is time constructible when $T(n) \ge n$ and some machine
can produce the binary representation of $T(|x|)$ from any input $x$ within a
constant multiple of $T(|x|) + 1$ steps. The main result restores the book's
first example under this definition: the identity function is time
constructible, witnessed by a four-state machine that maintains a
little-endian binary counter on its work tape with an amortized potential
argument, then emits the counter as output.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Time-constructible function]
\lean{Complexity.TimeConstructible}
\label{Complexity.TimeConstructible}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
A function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is \emph{time constructible} if
$n \le T(n)$ for every $n$, and there exist a positive integer constant $c$ and
a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet that, on every input word
$x \in \{0,1\}^{*}$, computes the binary representation of $T(|x|)$
(least-significant bit first, with no redundant leading zeros, so $0$ is
represented by the empty word) within at most $c \cdot (T(|x|) + 1)$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Increment of a little-endian binary word]
\lean{Complexity.counterInc}
\label{Complexity.counterInc}
\leanok
The successor operation on binary words written least-significant bit first:
the empty word maps to the single-bit word $1$; a word beginning with $0$ has
that bit set to $1$ and the rest unchanged; a word beginning with $1$ has that
bit cleared to $0$ and the increment carries recursively into the remaining
word.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Carry length of a binary word]
\lean{Complexity.counterCarry}
\label{Complexity.counterCarry}
\leanok
For a binary word written least-significant bit first, the number of leading
$1$ bits — that is, the number of cells cleared to $0$ when the word is
incremented. A word that is empty or begins with $0$ has carry length $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One-count identity for binary increment]
\lean{Complexity.counterInc_potential}
\label{Complexity.counterInc_potential}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCarry, Complexity.counterInc}
\difficulty{3}
For every finite binary word $b$ written least-significant bit first, the number of $1$
bits in its increment plus the number of leading $1$ bits in $b$ equals the number of
$1$ bits in $b$ plus one.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Increment of a binary representation]
\lean{Complexity.counterInc_bits}
\label{Complexity.counterInc_bits}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterInc}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, incrementing its least-significant-bit-first binary
representation produces the least-significant-bit-first binary representation of $n+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length bounds for binary increment]
\lean{Complexity.counterInc_length}
\label{Complexity.counterInc_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCarry, Complexity.counterInc}
\difficulty{3}
For every finite binary word $b$ written least-significant bit first, its increment has
length at most $|b|+1$, and the number of leading $1$ bits of $b$ is at most the length
of its increment.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Single carry transition action]
\lean{Complexity.counterBump}
\label{Complexity.counterBump}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Given an input-head displacement $d \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ and the symbol currently
scanned on the work tape, the action of one carry step of a one-work-tape
binary machine: if the scanned cell holds $1$, it is overwritten with $0$, the
work head moves right, and the machine continues in its carry state; otherwise
(a $0$ or a blank) the cell is overwritten with $1$, the work head moves left,
and the machine enters its rewind state. In both cases the input head moves by
$d$ and nothing is written to the output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The four-state binary-counter machine]
\lean{Complexity.counterTM}
\label{Complexity.counterTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterBump, Turing.FinTM}
A finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet with one work tape and four
states: \emph{count}, \emph{carry}, \emph{rewind}, and \emph{emit}. In the
count state it performs a carry transition while also advancing the input head,
or switches to the emit state when the input is exhausted. In the carry state
it propagates an increment along the work tape (clearing $1$s rightward until
it writes a $1$ over the first $0$ or blank). In the rewind state it moves the
work head left until it finds the blank at cell $-1$, then steps right to cell
$0$ and re-enters the count state. In the emit state it copies the work-tape
word to the output, one bit per step moving right, and halts at the first
blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tape of a finite binary word]
\lean{Complexity.counterTape}
\label{Complexity.counterTape}
\leanok
The work-tape contents determined by a finite binary word $b$: for an integer
position $z$, cell $z$ holds the $z$-th bit of $b$ when $0 \le z < |b|$, and is
blank at every other position (in particular at all negative positions).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Canonical counter configuration]
\lean{Complexity.counterCfg}
\label{Complexity.counterCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterTape, Turing.Cfg}
The configuration of the one-work-tape four-state counter machine on an input
word $x$ specified by: a state $q$ among the four counter states, an input-head
position $p$, an integer work-head position $z$, a finite binary word $b$ laid
out on the nonnegative cells of the work tape (blank elsewhere), and an output
word.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Reading after a binary prefix]
\lean{Complexity.counterTape_read}
\label{Complexity.counterTape_read}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterTape}
\difficulty{3}
For finite binary words $p$ and $b$, the tape formed by placing their concatenation on
the nonnegative cells has, at position $|p|$, the first bit of $b$, or a blank if $b$ is
empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Writing at a binary prefix boundary]
\lean{Complexity.counterTape_write}
\label{Complexity.counterTape_write}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterTape, Complexity.counterTape_read}
\difficulty{4}
For finite binary words $p$ and $b$ and a bit $eta$, overwrite position $|p|$ of the
tape containing their concatenation with $eta$. The resulting tape is the tape of the
word formed by appending $eta$ to $p$ and then appending the tail of $b$ (the word
obtained by removing its first bit, or the empty word if $b$ is empty).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Single step of the carry phase]
\lean{Complexity.counter_carry_step}
\label{Complexity.counter_carry_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterBump, Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterTape, Complexity.counterTape_read, Complexity.counterTape_write, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a finite binary input word, let $p$ be a valid input-head position for $x$,
and let $a,b$ be finite binary words. Starting in state $1$ with input-head position
$p$, work-head position $|a|$, the tape containing the concatenation of $a$ and $b$, and
empty output, one step of the four-state binary-counter machine has the following
effect: if $b$ begins with $1$, it enters state $1$, moves the work head right by one,
and changes the tape word to $a$ followed by $0$ and the tail of $b$; otherwise it
enters state $2$, moves the work head left by one, and changes the tape word to $a$
followed by $1$ and the tail of $b$. The input-head position remains $p$ and the output
remains empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Execution of the full carry phase]
\lean{Complexity.counter_carry}
\label{Complexity.counter_carry}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCarry, Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterInc, Complexity.counter_carry_step, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a finite binary input word, let $p$ be a valid input-head position for $x$,
and let $b$ and $u$ be finite binary words. For every prefix $a$ of $b$, if the
four-state binary-counter machine starts in state $1$ with input-head position $p$,
work-head position $|a|$, the tape containing the concatenation of $a$ and $b$, and
empty output, then after exactly one more step than the number of leading $1$ bits of
$b$, it is in state $2$ with input-head position $p$, work-head position $|a|$ plus the
number of leading $1$ bits of $b$ minus one, the tape containing the concatenation of
$a$ and the increment of $b$, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rewinding the work-tape head]
\lean{Complexity.counter_rewind}
\label{Complexity.counter_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterTape, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ and $b$ be finite binary words, let $p$ be any input-head position among the
$|x|+2$ positions, and let $j$ be a natural number with $j\le |b|$. Starting in the
rewind state with input head at $p$, work head at $j-1$, tape contents given by $b$, and
empty output, after $j+1$ steps the machine is in the count state with input head still
at $p$, work head at $0$, tape contents still given by $b$, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Equality of count and carry successors]
\lean{Complexity.counter_start}
\label{Complexity.counter_start}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterBump, Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterTape, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.inputSymbolInner, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $b$ be finite binary words, and let $i<|x|$. The one-step successor of the
configuration with count state, input head at position $i+1$, work head at $0$, tape
contents $b$, and empty output equals the one-step successor of the configuration with
carry state, input head at position $i+2$, work head at $0$, the same tape contents, and
empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One complete counter increment]
\lean{Complexity.counter_increment}
\label{Complexity.counter_increment}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCarry, Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterInc, Complexity.counterInc_length, Complexity.counter_carry, Complexity.counter_rewind, Complexity.counter_start, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $b$ be finite binary words, and let $i<|x|$. Starting in the count state
with the input head at position $i+1$, work head at $0$, tape contents given by $b$, and
empty output, after $2r+2$ steps, where $r$ is the carry length of $b$, the machine is
in the count state with input head at position $i+2$, work head at $0$, tape contents
given by the increment of $b$, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Amortized counter invariant]
\lean{Complexity.counter_count}
\label{Complexity.counter_count}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCarry, Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterInc_bits, Complexity.counterInc_potential, Complexity.counterTape, Complexity.counter_increment, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite binary input word $x$ and every natural number $i$ with $i\le |x|$,
there is a natural number $t$ such that $t+2w(i)\le4i$, where $w(i)$ is the number of
$1$ bits in the least-significant-bit-first binary representation of $i$, and after $t$
steps from the machine's initial configuration on $x$, the machine is in state $0$ with
input-head position $i+1$, work-head position $0$, the tape holding the binary
representation of $i$, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix emission during the emit phase]
\lean{Complexity.counter_emit_run}
\label{Complexity.counter_emit_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterTape, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $b$ be finite binary words, let $p$ be any input-head position among the
$|x|+2$ positions, and let $i$ be a natural number with $i\le |b|$. Starting in the emit
state with input head at $p$, work head at $0$, tape contents given by $b$, and empty
output, after $i$ steps the machine is in the emit state, with input head still at $p$,
work head at $i$, unchanged tape contents, and output equal to the prefix of $b$ of
length $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Emission halts with the stored word]
\lean{Complexity.counter_emit}
\label{Complexity.counter_emit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counterTape, Complexity.counter_emit_run, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ and $b$ be finite binary words, and let $p$ be any input-head position among the
$|x|+2$ positions. Starting the four-state counter machine in its emit state, with input
head at $p$, work head at $0$, tape contents given by $b$, and empty output, after
$|b|+1$ steps its state is halted and its output is $b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Identity Is Time Constructible]
\lean{Complexity.timeConstructible_id}
\label{Complexity.timeConstructible_id}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeConstructible, Complexity.counterCfg, Complexity.counter_count, Complexity.counter_emit, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.length_bits_le_self}
\difficulty{5}
The identity function $n\mapsto n$ on the natural numbers is time constructible: for
every natural number $n$, $n\le n$, and there exist a positive natural number $c$ and a
finite binary Turing machine that, on every binary input $x$, outputs the binary
representation of $|x|$ within $c(|x|+1)$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{definition}[Length-bits Turing machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.counterBump, Turing.FinTM}
The length-bits machine is the finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with one
work tape, four states, and initial state $0$. Its transition rule is the one specified
by the given construction, using counter-update actions in states $0$ and $1$; the
remaining states perform the stated tape scans, output symbols, and halting behavior.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Time bound for computing length bits]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM_computes}
\label{Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM_computes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM}
The finite Boolean Turing machine that outputs the binary bits of the input length
computes the function $x\mapsto \operatorname{bits}(|x|)$ in time $n\mapsto 5(n+1)$: for
every Boolean word $x$, it halts within $5(|x|+1)$ steps with output equal to the binary
representation of $|x|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space bound for length bits machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM_spaceUsed}
\label{Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM_spaceUsed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed}
For every Boolean word $x$ and every natural number $t$, the total number of work-tape
cells visited by the length-bits machine during the first $t$ steps of its computation
on $x$ is at most $5(\operatorname{size}(|x|)+1)$, where $\operatorname{size}$ is the
binary size of a natural number.
\end{theorem}
